items.claim: Pilot cohort (140 engineers, 12 weeks) accepted 61% of agent-suggested changes without material edits.
items.source: Internal pilot telemetry export, fixture CSV pilot_acceptance.csv

items.claim: Median time-to-merge for agent-assisted routine changes: 4.1 hours, vs. 9.6 hours cohort baseline.
items.source: Internal pilot telemetry export, fixture CSV pilot_cycle_time.csv

items.claim: Post-merge defect rate on agent-assisted changes: 3.2%, vs. 2.9% cohort baseline (not statistically distinguishable at pilot's n).
items.source: Internal pilot telemetry export, fixture CSV pilot_defect_rate.csv

items.claim: Pilot engineers logged an average of 6.4 agent invocations per working day.
items.source: Internal pilot telemetry export, fixture CSV pilot_usage.csv

items.claim: Pilot support desk logged 23 agent-related tickets over 12 weeks; 4 concerned suggested changes that would have introduced a regression.
items.source: Internal support ticket export, fixture CSV pilot_support_tickets.csv

items.claim: Pilot infrastructure cost (inference + tooling): GBP38,400 over 12 weeks for 140 seats.
items.source: Internal finance export, fixture CSV pilot_infra_cost.csv

items.claim: Pilot exit survey: 71% of participating engineers want continued access; 9% want to opt out entirely.
items.source: Internal pilot exit survey, fixture CSV pilot_exit_survey.csv

items.claim: Internal security review of the pilot found cost per accepted change of GBP0.72 in review overhead; secrets-handling controls were reviewed and passed; a prompt-injection concern via untrusted code comments was raised and left open pending a follow-up review.
items.source: Internal security review summary (de-impersonated per ADR-003 -- this is authored fixture content, not real Hekton Assurance output or any named real system's report)

items.claim: Industry survey of 400 engineering orgs: median reported coding-agent adoption at comparable scale is 34% of eligible engineers after 12 months, with wide variance by language/stack mix.
items.source: Fixture industry survey summary, engineering-tooling-adoption-2026.pdf

items.claim: Vendor-published benchmark claims 55% cycle-time reduction on greenfield tasks; benchmark methodology does not disclose task selection criteria.
items.source: Fixture vendor benchmark PDF, vendor-benchmark-2026.pdf

items.claim: Analyst note: enterprise coding-agent contracts in this band typically include a 15-20% annual list-price escalator after the first renewal.
items.source: Fixture analyst note, procurement-trends-2026.pdf

items.claim: Regulatory guidance published this quarter recommends (not yet mandates) documented human review of AI-suggested code changes to regulated systems before merge.
items.source: Fixture regulatory guidance summary, ai-code-review-guidance-2026.pdf

items.claim: Principal architect assessment: agent-suggested changes are strongest on well-tested, well-typed codebases and weakest on the legacy monolith's untyped modules, which cover roughly 30% of engineering headcount's day-to-day work.
items.source: Internal architecture review note (fixture)

items.claim: Engineering manager judgment across 6 teams: onboarding new engineers with agent access reduced time-to-first-merged-change, but managers could not isolate the agent's contribution from a concurrent onboarding-process change.
items.source: Internal manager survey note (fixture)

items.claim: CISO delegate judgment: current pilot scope did not exercise the agent against any system handling regulated customer data, so the security review's findings do not generalise to a full rollout without a further review.
items.source: Internal security delegate note (fixture)

items.claim: Finance projects fully-loaded support and platform-engineering cost to sustain a 5,000-seat rollout at GBP1.1m-1.6m annually, driven mainly by internal tooling integration work, not licence cost.
items.source: Internal finance forecast model (fixture)

items.claim: Adoption-curve forecast: at the pilot's observed opt-out rate, a targeted rollout to 1,200 engineers is projected to reach 65-75% active usage by month 6; an unrestricted enterprise rollout is projected to reach only 40-55% by month 6 due to weaker onboarding support per engineer.
items.source: Internal adoption forecast model (fixture)

items.claim: Assumed engineering productivity uplift from broad agent access: 18%, range 5-30%, extrapolated from the pilot's cycle-time reduction under an assumption that pilot conditions generalise to the wider engineering population.
items.source: Economics model input, not independently measured at rollout scale

items.claim: Assumed attrition-risk reduction from improved engineer experience: 1-2 percentage points off the current 14% annual voluntary attrition rate, based on the pilot exit survey's stated preference for continued access.
items.source: Economics model input, not independently measured

items.claim: Assumed training and change-management cost per engineer onboarded: GBP340, based on the pilot's per-seat onboarding spend.
items.source: Economics model input, not independently measured at scale

items.claim: Assumed licence unit cost holds flat for 24 months before any renewal escalator applies, despite ev-011's analyst note on typical escalator timing.
items.source: Economics model input, a simplifying assumption the model does not currently relax

items.claim: Inferred from ev-002 and ev-004 together: engineers who invoke the agent more than 5 times per day show a larger median cycle-time reduction than low-frequency users, suggesting usage intensity, not mere access, drives most of the benefit.
items.source: Internal analysis of pilot telemetry (fixture), not itself a direct measurement

items.claim: Inferred from ev-009 (industry adoption survey) and ev-017 (internal adoption forecast): this organisation's projected adoption trajectory sits below the reported industry median, consistent with its higher share of legacy/untyped codebase per ev-013.
items.source: Internal analysis (fixture), a cross-reference inference, not a new measurement

items.claim: No agreed methodology exists yet for attributing observed cycle-time or defect-rate changes at enterprise scale specifically to agent usage versus concurrent process changes (see ev-014).
items.source: Gap identified during pilot review; no source resolves this

items.claim: Long-run behaviour of agent-suggested code quality as the underlying model provider updates its model version is not established; the pilot ran on a single fixed model version throughout.
items.source: Gap identified during pilot review; no source resolves this

items.claim: Real-world incident rate for the open prompt-injection concern (ev-008) at full rollout scale is unknown; the pilot recorded zero exploited incidents, but pilot scope and duration may be too limited to observe a low-frequency event.
items.source: Gap identified during security review; no source resolves this
